prompt:
Continue this exact laparoscopic cholecystectomy footage for 10 seconds. Same camera, viewpoint, lighting, colours, image quality and anatomy as the input image.

What is in the scene (taken from the real frame):
A circular laparoscopic view shows a gallbladder dissection with three metallic instruments. On the right, a reddish-brown liver lobe has pale yellowish patches. To the left, a bluish-grey gallbladder with dark vessels is encased in yellow fat. A silver grasper with black shaft bands and serrated, fenestrated jaws enters from the lower right, grasping tissue in a dissected window at the gallbladder base. Another silver grasper enters from the lower left, holding fatty tissue at the gallbladder neck. A third metallic shaft enters from the top center, retracting the upper gallbladder fat. Dark pooled fluid is visible at the bottom, and there is no active bleeding, smoke, or surgical clips.

One surgical step happens (chosen by a patient world model): A laparoscopic clip applier: a long shaft with two jaws holding one small metal clip comes into view along its shaft (or, if it is already in view, moves to the cystic duct). It closes its jaws across the cystic duct, leaving one small metal clip on it, then opens and withdraws.

Instruments already in view: the grasper and the scissors. An instrument never changes into another instrument. Before the clipper arrives, any instrument in its way slides straight back out of view along its own shaft; the others stay where they are.

By the end of the clip: the cystic duct has 1 small metal clip across it.

Motion: slow, small, physically plausible movements only. The camera stays at the same distance and angle with very slight handheld drift. Instruments keep their exact shape, colour, size and entry side. Tissue moves only where an instrument touches it, deforms slightly and springs back.

Keep identical to the input image for the whole clip: the colours, the lighting, the image grain and sharpness, the circular endoscope vignette, and every anatomical structure not named above.

Strictly forbidden: new, extra, swapped or reshaped instruments; a new sac or organ appearing; smoke; zooms, camera cuts or jumps; text or overlays; changes of colour, exposure or image quality; human hands; bleeding; cutting.

Following clip application, the surgeon retracts the gallbladder with a grasper in four of the five reference cases, or grasps the cystic duct in the remaining case (VID110_00901).
